utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Peter McCloskey. And with me today is Janet Stewart, Stacy de la Torre, Stefan Waespi, and Anne Davis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, members of the Court. I am David Wilson. Seated with me today is Mr. Dusan Slijepcevic, co-counsel. We are the attorneys for Mr. Obrenovic in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Obrenovic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED OBRENOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear and understand everything that's being said in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you get interpretation? Oh, I'm sorry. Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Well, good morning, ladies and gentlemen. The Trial Chamber is seized with a joint motion for consideration of plea agreement between Dragan Obrenovic and the Office of the Prosecutor. This motion was filed jointly by the counsel for Mr. Obrenovic and the Prosecution on the 20th of May, 2003. According to the plea agreement attached to the joint motion, the accused Obrenovic agrees to plead guilty to count 5 of the amended joint indictment dated 27th May 2002 as a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(H) of the Statute of the Tribunal. The plea agreement contains provisions reflecting the understanding of the accused Obrenovic as to the nature of count 5, including legal elements of persecution as a crime against humanity, and the factual basis agreed upon as a base -- as a basis for his guilty plea to this count. The plea agreement also recommends a range of sentences based on an understanding that such recommendation is not binding on the Trial Chamber. The Office of the Prosecutor agrees to move to dismiss the remaining charges against Dragan Obrenovic set out in the indictment at the time of the acceptance of the plea by the Trial Chamber without prejudice to either party. The Trial Chamber has observed that the plea agreement has also been in B/C/S language, which the accused Obrenovic understands, and is attached to the joint motion. The Trial Chamber also looked at the provisions of the relevant Rules, in particular Rule 62 bis and Rule 62 ter. We'll proceed in accordance with these Rules. Since we just got the agreement yesterday, maybe first of all I would like to invite the parties to brief us on the contents of the plea agreement. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Initially, I'd like to point out the timing of this agreement, which is always an important factor when the Prosecution considers the benefit to the Prosecution and to the victims. And in this case, it was communicated to the Prosecution that Mr. Obrenovic had taken responsibility for his actions, as pointed out in count 5, prior to the start of the trial, after the plea of Momir Nikolic but prior to the start of the trial. And we were able to after that initial acknowledgment reach the plea agreement that you see today. So the Prosecutor would like this plea agreement to be considered a pre-trial agreement as for timing purposes. For the actual plea agreement, it -- basically, Mr. Obrenovic is admitting to count 5 of the indictment, crime against humanity, persecutions, which includes the murders and the various other allegations laid out in the indictment. And we are -- we will be dismissing the other counts. The Prosecution will be recommending, pursuant to Mr. Obrenovic's continued cooperation, that a sentence of 15 to 20 years is the appropriate sentence. And Mr. Obrenovic has promised to testify truthfully at any trial related to Srebrenica 1995 that he has evidence on, as requested by the Prosecution. These are the fundamental points of the plea agreement, and I am confident, as I'm sure Mr. Wilson and Mr. Obrenovic are, that this was done carefully and freely and voluntarily. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any comments, anything to add on the part of the Defence team? Mr. Wilson.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, members of the panel. First I would say that Mr. McCloskey's general outline of the plea agreement is accurate and it does set forth the most important and most central portions of the plea agreement. Mr. Slijepcevic and I would like to say that we have been Mr. Obrenovic's attorneys for two years. We have reviewed all of the discovery materials, hundreds of thousands of pages provided us by the Prosecution. We have visited the alleged crime scenes that are set out in the indictment. We have conducted our own investigation. We have interviewed dozens of witnesses. We have thoroughly studied the jurisprudence of the Tribunal as it applies to these charges. We have spent hundreds of hours in conference with Mr. Obrenovic about this case. We have spent dozens of hours in conference with Mr. Obrenovic about the subject of this plea agreement. We have thoroughly discussed his options of going to trial or pleading guilty. We have answered all of his questions to the best of our ability and we believe that he has understood our answers and that he is fully informed about the nature of the process that he has begun today. We have always told him that the decision must be his alone and that we would support him as to either option he chose. He is aware that we were prepared to go forward with trial, present an active defence. He is also aware that we would continue to support him in satisfying his obligations under this agreement and in representing him through the conclusions of these proceedings as they relate to him. It is in this context that he is entering his plea of guilty today, and it's because of this context that we respect his decision as being one which was arrived at voluntarily on his part, with the advice of counsel, and after thorough discussions and considerations of all the factors that he should have considered. And it is for this reason that we are satisfied in our own minds that Mr. Obrenovic's actions today are voluntary, that he is well informed, and that he understands what is going on. If the Court has any other questions, we will be happy to answer them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, I think the Judges will have some questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: My question to both parties: Why a sentencing range of the plea agreement of Nikolic and this plea agreement are the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- there are certain factors that we took into account. One of the primary factors was the timing of the -- of the plea. Both persons pled before trial. And we viewed a captain, Mr. Nikolic, as a security officer who was a security officer by choice, who was charged with genocide. And we looked at Mr. Obrenovic as a chief of staff deputy commander who was not charged with genocide. And while it's my view that a commander bears more responsibility than a staff officer, we also viewed this as a person that was only temporarily in command and whose commander should bear the brunt -- not the brunt but a significant part of the command responsibility for these atrocious crimes, and that we believe that 15 to 20 years in the context of European law and the law of Yugoslavia is a significant sentence and that the victims of this crime, those that I have been speaking to on the telephone that are afraid to come in, that don't want to come in but will come in, are -- are benefitted by this. And the Prosecution is also benefitted by hearing the truthful account of Mr. Obrenovic, which we believe we have provided before you, where he has admitted taking responsibility, military responsibility for accepting the murder operation of thousands. And we believe that -- that 15 to 20 years is fair, in terms of a range. Now, we're talking ranges for both of them, and we believe that is fair and it is within the general framework of the discussions that have been ongoing with both parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: In para 4 of the plea agreement, in (a), part (a), it is said that the accused will make his sentencing recommendation upon the filing of this -- of his pre-sentence memorandum. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, you have noticed from the Nikolic plea that the Nikolic Defence chose to make their recommendation of ten years in the plea agreement. That was their recommendation. That was not the Prosecution's recommendation. That was the Nikolic recommendation. And this -- Mr. Obrenovic and his Defence counsel chose to make this particular statement and retain the right to provide you their recommendations at a later date. And from that point I will turn over anything further to Mr. Wilson.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. McCloskey accurately states our request. We stated to him that we would prefer to retain the right to make a recommendation to you with our sentencing memorandum. We would like to see how events progress. There is a great deal of work to be done before sentencing is reached in this case, and we felt that it was not necessary or appropriate for us at this time to indicate what our sentencing recommendation would be. We, of course, understand that that would be our recommendation and the Court is free to proceed as it sees fit. But from our standpoint, we did not want to make a recommendation at this point. Mr. Nikolic chose different. We respect his reasons, but our thinking on it was different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, to my understanding, that at least paragraph 14 will be a kind of agreement between the parties. Am I right? I think that's the minimum agreement between the parties concerning with the sentence issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 14, we believe, does clearly state the agreement of the parties, Your Honour, and Mr. Obrenovic understands that. That's our understanding of what we're doing today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. We have gone over each of these paragraphs, and both sides fully agree and support them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Concerning with paragraph 5, which maybe involved the amendment of the indictment in the future, and it's also related to other co-accused in this case, Mr. McCloskey, are you going to file another application for the third amended indictment, and when are you going to do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Mr. President. As this agreement basically voids the filing of the -- of the indictment that didn't have Mr. Nikolic on it, we will endeavour to as soon as possible file another indictment that incorporates these few changes and does not have Mr. Nikolic or Mr. Obrenovic on it. Of course, depending on your acceptance of -- of this -- of this plea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the purpose for that is to give the opportunity for other co-accused, the opportunity to -- to make their response if they believe that certain amendments in that indictment related to their crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely, and we are in the process and have a draft of that new indictment, and it shouldn't be long in coming. We'll be able to give you a more detailed view when that will come. We're -- we're working on our adjudicated facts motion and other motions as well, but it -- this new indictment should come in very soon. I would hope before the end of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On the paragraph 9, you mentioned proffer agreement, and we have not seen any filing of those proffer agreement. Could I know what's the exact meaning of this proffer agreement? Is this same with that filed in the Nikolic case, or is it a general statement of facts or terms of the future statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, yesterday - and you haven't obviously received it yet - we did file the proffer agreement as we had in Nikolic to be consistent, so that you would see that it's basically the same procedures are in place here. It's basically the same agreement. And we just chose at this -- in this agreement to put it in the agreement so that it was clear to -- to the parties and the Court what precisely occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just got it. Well, it seems to me that the Judges have exhausted their questions. Could I now address to the accused, Mr. Obrenovic, at this stage. Mr. Obrenovic, the Trial Chamber would like to find out from you whether you understand the details of this plea agreement you entered into with the Prosecution. THE ACCUSED OBRENOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I fully understand. I have discussed and studied this with my Defence team, and I have a full understanding of what is stated therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And this Trial Chamber would like also to find out from you when entering into this plea agreement, you understand that the Trial Chamber is not bound to accept the range of sentence agreed by yourself and the Prosecution. THE ACCUSED OBRENOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we also would like to ask you whether you fully discussed with your counsel the plea agreement and he advised you of the consequences of pleading guilty to count 5, that is, persecution. THE ACCUSED OBRENOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This Trial Chamber would like to know whether you are threatened or coerced in any way to make this agreement. Was it entirely made by you voluntarily? THE ACCUSED OBRENOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was never threatened or coerced. This is entirely of my own free will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At this stage I would like to have Madam Registrar to read paragraph 59 of the indictment, that is, the contents of the persecutions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "As described in this Amended Joinder Indictment, the crime of persecutions was perpetrated, executed, and carried out by and through the following means: a) the murder of thousands of Bosnian Muslim civilians, including men, women, children, and elderly persons; b) the cruel and inhumane treatment of Bosnian Muslim civilians, including severe beatings at Potocari and in detention facilities in Bratunac and Zvornik; c) the terrorising of Bosnian Muslim civilians in Srebrenica and at Potocari; d) the destruction of personal property and effects belonging to the Bosnian Muslims; and e) the forcible transfer of Bosnian Muslims from the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to put the count to you so that you can plea as advised and according to your own free will, that is, count 5 of the charges, as detailed in the plea agreement. How do you plea to count 5 of the amended indictment, charging you with persecution as a crime against humanity; guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED OBRENOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my plea is guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well. The Trial Chamber records the plea of guilty or count 5, persecution, by the accused. You may sit down, please. The Trial Chamber has considered the particulars of the facts in the plea agreement and is satisfied that they do form sufficient factual basis for finding the accused guilty on this count, and therefore makes a finding of guilty and enters the conviction for count 5, persecution, against the accused, Mr. Obrenovic. We also accept the plea agreement with the understanding that the Prosecutor will move to dismiss without prejudice to either party the remaining charges against Dragan Obrenovic set out in the indictment. The Trial Chamber will issue orders relating further proceedings in due course. Now we would like to move to the next stage, about possible date for hearing of sentencing and would like to find out from both parties how they intend to make their submissions on sentencing and when. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, ideally we'd do this jointly with the Nikolic sentencing, just for efficiency and the time frames that you have set out and that are workable for the Prosecution. But we would not object if the Defence needs some more time in that regard. We're -- we're very open to the Court and counsel on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could I hear the response from Mr. Wilson.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are also quite flexible, if the Court decides to do those sentencings at the same time, we of course will prepare for it on whatever schedule the Court sets. There's a question in my mind and perhaps Mr. McCloskey knows at this time or perhaps he doesn't, as to when these two individuals would be ready for sentencing, that is, when they will have testified or be ready to go forward, whether the two defendants will be testifying near to each other in the stage of the trial or whether we are talking about different periods of time. So we are quite flexible for whatever time the Court sets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe Mr. McCloskey could shed some light on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would still like to have Mr. Nikolic and Mr. Obrenovic testify before the summer break. I'm hoping that's realistic. As you can imagine, we're in the process of reassessing our case, our 92 bis motions, our -- our factual motions regarding adjudicated facts. And I would like to get this done prior to the summer break, and I think I can do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Trial Chamber are take into consideration the views expressed by both parties and issue a scheduling order on matters for further hearing in this procedure. I think that's all. We are adjourned.
